extracted_claims.text: The original EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) set the application date for the high-risk AI obligations listed in Annex III (Chapter III, Sections 1-3) at 2 August 2026.
The 'AI Omnibus'/Digital Omnibus on AI amendment extended the application date for Annex III high-risk AI obligations from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027.
The AI Omnibus amending regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026, after a political agreement reached on 7 May 2026 and legislative proposal adopted on 19 November 2025.
As amended, Article 113(c)(i) of the AI Act provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (covering Annex III high-risk systems), except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027.

High-risk AI systems that are safety components of, or themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I will become subject to obligations from 2 August 2028 (previously 2 August 2027 under the original Act).
The amending regulation implementing the delay is referred to as Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.

Operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III will only become subject to the Regulation if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date, with public-authority deployers required to take necessary steps regardless.

Before the Omnibus amendment, the Commission had proposed adjusting the timeline for high-risk AI rules by up to 16 months so that application would begin once the Commission confirmed that needed standards and tools were available, rather than on a fixed calendar date.

Some commentary and industry guidance published as late as April 2026 continued to describe 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline for Annex III high-risk obligations, treating the delay as uncertain or not yet finalized.
As of publications referencing the entry into force of the Omnibus (27 July 2026) and later, the current, binding deadline for Annex III high-risk AI obligations is 2 December 2027.

# When Do EU AI Act Obligations for Annex III High-Risk AI Systems Apply?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (Chapter III, Sections 1–3) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, a subsequent "AI Omnibus" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, has pushed this deadline to **2 December 2027** ([AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [32024R1689 — EN — 27.07.2026](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). This is now the current, binding deadline, though some earlier publications still reference the original 2026 date.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Framework
The original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3 obligations governing Annex III high-risk AI systems (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [EU AI Act Timeline: Key Dates](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and New Deadline
The Digital/AI Omnibus amendment extended the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This amendment entered into force on 27 July 2026, following a political agreement reached on 7 May 2026 and a legislative proposal adopted on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). As amended, Article 113(c)(i) now provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (excluding Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [32024R1689 — EN — 27.07.2026](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). As of publications referencing the Omnibus's entry into force and later, 2 December 2027 is confirmed as the current binding deadline (high confidence) ([AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [EU AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

### Related Transitional Dates
High-risk AI systems that are safety components of, or themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) will become subject to obligations from 2 August 2028, delayed from the original 2 August 2027 date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Operators of high-risk systems already placed on the market or in service before Chapter III's application date only become subject to the Regulation if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward, though public-authority deployers must act regardless (high confidence) ([Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [32024R1689 — EN — 27.07.2026](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Precursor Proposals
Before the Omnibus was finalized, the Commission had proposed adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that application would begin once standards and tools were confirmed available, rather than on a fixed date (medium confidence) ([Council and Parliament agree to simplify rules](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting pre-Omnibus publication dates rather than a substantive disagreement ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)). Similarly, the Annex I product-embedded transition date appears as both 2 August 2027 (pre-Omnibus) and 2 August 2028 (post-Omnibus) depending on publication timing ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) vs. [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The claim that the amending regulation is formally numbered "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is flagged as **low confidence** and unconfirmed by authoritative EU sources ([EU AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Likewise, commentary suggesting the August 2026 deadline remained uncertain as late as April 2026 is **low confidence** and now superseded ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)).

## Knowledge Gaps
The official Official Journal citation for the Omnibus amendment is not confirmed across sources. It remains unclear whether the final text retained conditionality tied to standards-readiness or set an unconditional date. Sources do not clarify whether all Chapter III sub-obligations (conformity assessment, registration, post-market monitoring) uniformly shift to 2 December 2027, nor how the Article 111 "significant design changes" trigger interacts with the new date for legacy systems. Practical compliance implications for organizations that prepared for the original 2026 deadline are not addressed.

# When Do EU AI Act Obligations for Annex III High-Risk AI Systems Apply?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (Chapter III, Sections 1–3) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113)). However, a subsequent "AI Omnibus" amendment, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, has pushed this deadline to **2 December 2027** ([AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force), [32024R1689 — EN — 27.07.2026](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). This is now the current, binding deadline, though some earlier publications still reference the original 2026 date.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Framework
The original Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 set 2 August 2026 as the application date for Chapter III, Sections 1–3 obligations governing Annex III high-risk AI systems (medium confidence) ([Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [EU AI Act Timeline: Key Dates](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)).

### The Omnibus Amendment and New Deadline
The Digital/AI Omnibus amendment extended the Annex III application date from 2 August 2026 to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act), [AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This amendment entered into force on 27 July 2026, following a political agreement reached on 7 May 2026 and a legislative proposal adopted on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). As amended, Article 113(c)(i) now provides that Chapter III, Sections 1, 2 and 3 (excluding Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 (high confidence) ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [32024R1689 — EN — 27.07.2026](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)). As of publications referencing the Omnibus's entry into force and later, 2 December 2027 is confirmed as the current binding deadline (high confidence) ([AI Act | Shaping Europe's digital future](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [EU AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

### Related Transitional Dates
High-risk AI systems that are safety components of, or themselves, products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) will become subject to obligations from 2 August 2028, delayed from the original 2 August 2027 date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Navigating the AI Act](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act)). Operators of high-risk systems already placed on the market or in service before Chapter III's application date only become subject to the Regulation if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward, though public-authority deployers must act regardless (high confidence) ([Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [32024R1689 — EN — 27.07.2026](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Precursor Proposals
Before the Omnibus was finalized, the Commission had proposed adjusting the timeline by up to 16 months so that application would begin once standards and tools were confirmed available, rather than on a fixed date (medium confidence) ([Council and Parliament agree to simplify rules](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline, reflecting pre-Omnibus publication dates rather than a substantive disagreement ([CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20) vs. [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)). Similarly, the Annex I product-embedded transition date appears as both 2 August 2027 (pre-Omnibus) and 2 August 2028 (post-Omnibus) depending on publication timing ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act) vs. [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)). The claim that the amending regulation is formally numbered "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is flagged as **low confidence** and unconfirmed by authoritative EU sources ([EU AI Act Annex III Deadline 2027](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass timeline](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)). Likewise, commentary suggesting the August 2026 deadline remained uncertain as late as April 2026 is **low confidence** and now superseded ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO), [Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)).

## Knowledge Gaps
The official Official Journal citation for the Omnibus amendment is not confirmed across sources. It remains unclear whether the final text retained conditionality tied to standards-readiness or set an unconditional date. Sources do not clarify whether all Chapter III sub-obligations (conformity assessment, registration, post-market monitoring) uniformly shift to 2 December 2027, nor how the Article 111 "significant design changes" trigger interacts with the new date for legacy systems. Practical compliance implications for organizations that prepared for the original 2026 deadline are not addressed.
